questions.stem: This echocardiogram from a cyanotic neonate shows an aorta positioned above and straddling the interventricular septum, sitting over a septal defect. Which cyanotic congenital heart defect does this image represent?

explanation.summary: The echo demonstrates the overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect that are two of the four components of tetralogy of Fallot; the other two, pulmonary valve stenosis and RV hypertrophy, complete the tetrad.
explanation.whyCorrect: The echo demonstrates the overriding aorta and ventricular septal defect that are two of the four components of tetralogy of Fallot; the other two, pulmonary valve stenosis and RV hypertrophy, complete the tetrad.

questions.stem: This cardiac MR angiogram from an infant shows an enlarged right atrium, a markedly hypoplastic right ventricle, and no inlet from the RA to the RV. Which lesion does this represent?

explanation.summary: Absence of the tricuspid valve prevents RA-to-RV filling, so the RV receives little blood and becomes hypoplastic while the RA enlarges, the imaging hallmark of tricuspid atresia.
explanation.whyCorrect: Absence of the tricuspid valve prevents RA-to-RV filling, so the RV receives little blood and becomes hypoplastic while the RA enlarges, the imaging hallmark of tricuspid atresia.

questions.stem: A neonate with a right-to-left shunt shows the bluish discoloration seen here in the nailbeds, fingers, and toes. This clinical sign results directly from an increased blood concentration of what?

explanation.summary: Cyanosis becomes visible when the absolute amount of reduced (deoxygenated) hemoglobin in the blood rises above roughly 5 g/dL, which occurs when a right-to-left shunt allows deoxygenated blood to bypass the lungs and enter the systemic circulation.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cyanosis becomes visible when the absolute amount of reduced (deoxygenated) hemoglobin in the blood rises above roughly 5 g/dL, which occurs when a right-to-left shunt allows deoxygenated blood to bypass the lungs and enter the systemic circulation.

questions.stem: This schematic shows a single arterial trunk arising from the heart that then divides into the aorta and pulmonary arteries. Failure of which embryologic process produces this defect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Failure of the truncoconal septum to divide the outflow tract

choices.label: B
choices.text: Failure of the endocardial cushions to fuse

choices.label: C
choices.text: Failure of the interventricular foramen to close

choices.label: D
choices.text: Failure of the sinus venosus to be incorporated

choices.label: E
choices.text: Failure of the septum primum and secundum to fuse

explanation.summary: Normally the truncoconal septum spirals down to separate the aorta from the pulmonary trunk; when this division fails, a single truncal vessel overrides both ventricles, defining persistent truncus arteriosus.
explanation.whyCorrect: Normally the truncoconal septum spirals down to separate the aorta from the pulmonary trunk; when this division fails, a single truncal vessel overrides both ventricles, defining persistent truncus arteriosus.
